[TASK: 2560x1440 2K QHD 16:9 ARCHITECTURAL RELIGHTING & STATIC RECONSTRUCTION]
Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic 6x7 medium-format architectural survey photograph.

MANDATORY TRANSFORMATION RULES:
1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. Plumb all vertical walls to true gravity vertical. Render razor-sharp ashlar courses, straight timber sash mullions, and crisp slate roofs.
2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the carriageway with authentic road surfacing, stone setts, whinstone kerbs, and clean flagstone pavements.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   - Botanical Classification: Urban parkland canopy in Drummond Place Gardens dominated by *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore maple), *Ulmus glabra* (Wych elm), *Fagus sylvatica* (Common beech), *Platanus × acerifolia* (London plane), and *Tilia × europaea* (Common lime).
- Phenology (November 11): Advanced late-autumn defoliation state (approximately 75–85% leaf loss); exposed dendritic branch architecture, sparse clinging russet, dull amber, and bronze foliage across inner crowns; dense understory carpets of fallen decaying leaf litter across lawn turf.
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Pin-sharp infinite depth of field (f/11). Zero lens blur, tilt-shift, or depth-of-field falloff across foreground and background.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
SOLAR LIGHT VECTOR (4500K Late afternoon raking sunlight with warm golden highlights): Sun at camera-left (Azimuth 187.5°, Elevation 16.5°). left walls in direct sun, right walls in deep shadow. long lateral shadows project across ground to RIGHT.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
Medium format 6x7 architectural survey of London Street looking west toward Drummond Place Gardens, Edinburgh New Town. Continuous 4-storey late Georgian residential terraces flanked on both sides, built from fine-jointed Craigleith buff sandstone with channelled rustication on ground floors and smooth-polished ashlar on upper storeys. Moulded stringcourses, prominent eaves cornices, and pitched Ballachulish slate roofs punctuated by massive ashlar chimney stacks with rows of cylindrical terracotta pots. Deep basement lightwells protected by black-painted spear-head cast-iron railings and stone plinths. Rectangular fenestration arranged in uniform vertical grids of white-painted timber sash-and-case windows (6-over-6 and 2-over-2 panes) set into deep ashlar reveals. Natural historical coal-smoke carbon patina and rain-washed streaks across porous stone facades. In the middle ground, Drummond Place Gardens contains mature Acer pseudoplatanus, Fagus sylvatica, and Ulmus glabra in mid-November late-autumn senescence, featuring stark bare dendritic branch silhouettes with sparse residual russet foliage. Entire street clear of vehicles, traffic, pedestrians, and refuse; pristine Caithness flagstone pavements, granite kerbstones, and tarmacadam carriageway bordered by cast-iron streetlamps. Distant neoclassical tenement rooflines of the northern New Town extend horizontally into the background. Absolute planar facade rectification, zero lens distortion, deep focus edge-to-edge.
